title: Window-blind cords can strangle a child, so CPSC prefers cordless coverings
summary: CPSC says children can wrap blind cords around the neck, and it says to use cordless window coverings where young children live.
body: CPSC says cordless window coverings help prevent strangulation in homes with young children. A child can wrap a cord around the neck, or pull a cord that is hard to see and become caught in a loop. If corded coverings cannot be replaced, the page says to call the Window Covering Safety Council at 800-506-4636 for a free repair kit in the United States. That line is a product-repair number, not an emergency number. The page also says tension devices do not fix a dangling pull cord, and that dangling cords should be made as short as possible. Cribs should not sit against those cords. This is prevention. It is not a rescue procedure.
